exclusion_reason: SET-03: excluded from BAC120 inference. Task 03 recovered only 40 unique BAC120 markers with automatic translation table 4 and 43 with table 11, against 110-119 for the other 79 draft genomes; it is the single row in the Task 06 review-holds table; GTDB R232 independently records it as QC-failed (marker percentage, and NCBI "unverified source organism; many frameshifted proteins"). Its archived sequence is byte-identical to the current NCBI assembly, so the defect is in the record, not the local copy. Excluded from all three methods rather than BAC120 alone, so that the three receive the same tip set.

SET-20: excluded from phylogenetic inference by Michael on 23 September 2026, on Task 11's evidence. The only translation-table-4 genome in the 1,090-genome full cohort: GTDB-Tk recovers 44 of 120 unique BAC120 markers against a cohort median of 118, and the public NCBI record reports CheckM completeness 12.81% (contamination 0.22%) on a 5,028,240-bp assembly labelled Complete Genome. The same signature as SET-03 (GCA_002356475.1). An assembly-quality exclusion, not a naming decision; archived labels are unchanged. Removed by pruning the inferred trees rather than re-inferring them, following the pilot-decision rule; Task 11's leave-out sensitivity had already shown it moves no concordance figure.

exclusion_reason: Chimeric assembly; new exclusion made by this task. NCBI flags GCA_041890495.1 "contaminated" and "annotation fails completeness check" - the only "contaminated" note among the 389 candidate panel accessions - with taxonomy check Inconclusive/mismatch. Its best NCBI ANI match is Escherichia coli GCA_000210475.1 at 96.3% over only 46.6%/45.5% coverage, while 64.9% of it matches the E. hormaechei subsp. oharae type at 83.9%. Task 04 measured 90.52% ANI at 50.80% minimum aligned fraction to the E. quasiroggenkampii type: an intermediate identity at about half coverage, the signature of one record holding sequence from two genera. That also explains why GTDB R232 lists this exact accession as a tip in s__Escherichia boydii while the archived Kraken R220 label is E. quasiroggenkampii and the NCBI label is E. hormaechei - three classifiers each answering for a different part of the same file. 119 unique BAC120 markers do not clear it: a 5.2 Mb chimera still carries one copy of most single-copy markers, and a concatenated BAC120 alignment would then mix two genera inside one taxon while Verticall would read a whole-genome assembly artefact as recombination. The archived chromosome is sequence-identical to the current NCBI record (5,197,128 bp, 1 contig), so this is a defect in the public record, not the local copy. This is an assembly-quality exclusion, not a naming decision: the record is retained in provenance and is evidence for DEC-008 and the Task 12 case register.
